title: Dual-Rate Diffusion: Accelerating diffusion models with an interleaved heavy-light network
claim: A heavy network runs only at sparse steps and its features are reused by a light model at every step.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; generation (left) and training (right), image strip below
description: Two panels split by a vertical line. The left panel shows the generative process. A row of green circular nodes (x, z_t1 ... z_t6, z_1) sits above a strip of a dog image going from clean to pure noise. Blue boxes labeled g_θ sit above each node. Two large purple E_θ boxes sit at the top, each emitting a red embedding box (e_t3, e_1). Red arrows fan the embedding out to several g_θ boxes, so one heavy call serves many light steps. Green arrows carry the sample state up to E_θ, and blue arrows lead each step to the next, less noisy state. The right panel shows training with a single E_θ, e_τ, g_θ, x̂, and the noising chain x → z_t → z_τ. Dashed arrows are labeled q(z_t|x) and q(z_τ|z_t). Three dog images, clean to noisy, sit at the bottom. The eye goes first to the large purple E_θ boxes and the red fan-out arrows.
caption: Overview of Dual-Rate Diffusion generative process (on the left) and training (on the right). The context encoder $E_\Th$ (heavy network) is evaluated at sparse intervals to extract high-dimensional features, which are then reused by the light denoising model $g_\th$ at every step to refine the sample.
abstract: Diffusion models achieve state-of-the-art generative performance but suffer from high computational costs during inference due to the repeated evaluation of a heavy neural network. In this work, we propose Dual-Rate Diffusion, a method to accelerate sampling by interleaving the execution of a heavy high-capacity context encoder and a light efficient denoising model. The context encoder is evaluated sparsely to extract high-dimensional features, which are effectively reused by the light denoising model at every step to refine the sample efficiently. This approach significantly accelerates inference without compromising sample quality. On ImageNet benchmarks, Dual-Rate Diffusion matches the performance of standard baselines while reducing computational cost by a factor of $2$-$4$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our method is compatible with distillation techniques, such as Moment Matching Distillation, enabling further efficiency gains in few-step generation.
